# Preserve transport policy across an OH HTTP adapter change

## Platform difference

Replacing a native HTTP backend for OH can require explicit propagation of options through every application transport path.

## Implementation

Venera routes OH requests through dart:io instead of rhttp. Later WebDAV changes add per-endpoint TLS policy and then repair upload/download construction that had omitted the option even though connection testing supplied it. ConnSSH, SSH Codex and Minecraft Box keep their SSH/socket protocols in Dart, showing that a native network rewrite is not inherently required.

## Applicability

Apply policy consistently to probes, listing, uploads and downloads. Test proxy, cancellation, timeout and certificate behavior against the app's actual backend.

These observations apply to the pinned project revisions below, studied on 2026-09-30 and backfilled on 2026-10-06. Unspecified SDK/device compatibility remains unknown; this is not a fresh upstream assessment.

## Pitfalls and limitations

The Venera history records certificate-validation bypass support; bypass is a project option, not a recommended solution for ordinary TLS failures or an OH requirement. A successful connection test does not verify the data-transfer clients.

## Verification

Use valid and invalid certificates and exercise all transport paths. Verify defaults remain strict and that endpoint-specific configuration neither disappears nor leaks into unrelated clients.

Evidence tier: historical source/diff studies, with commit and path existence rechecked in local Git during this backfill. No application build, dependency resolution, signing, installation or device execution was performed. Proposed checks above are acceptance criteria, not completed tests.
